intermission_quips: Corp resets the table. Same rules, meaner bots. That's the fun part.
Your paint's holding up better than my first bot's did. Who would have known acetone melts paint?
Somebody's mom called asking if this is 'that gambling game.' It's not. It's a far more expensive vice. It's a HOBBY.
Trainer AI's been muttering about you in its logs. That's a compliment.
Loose tile on lane three, watch your footing. The bots won't.
Remember. It is only a game, and assault WILL get you banned from the store. Keep it on the table.
Closed Wednesdays for FightShovel 1920.
PixBot Market - Thursday Night."
10:00 PM, You don't have to go home, but you can't stay here.
Consider Ink Wash."
Jump-Jets allow your Pixel Bot to survive water levels.
Combine different synergies for unique effects.
The meta is a suggestion. Play what makes you happy, as long as it wins.
No running in the shop. I don't care if you're excited about your new missile launcher.
I just got a shipment of new chassis parts. First come, first served.
Don't tap on the arena glass. The AI hates it.
Some people play chess. We play chess with lasers and acid.
I'm thinking of hosting a 2v2 tournament next month. Find a partner.
If you smell smoke, your bot is overheating. Or the microwave in the back is broken again.
Respect your opponent. Even if they run a pure stalling deck.
Yes, the rumors are true. The Corp is watching these matches. No, I don't know why.
Every piece of scrap is a potential upgrade if you squint hard enough.
The stealth bot always gets you when you blink.
There is no 'luck' in PixBots. Just probability and poor planning.
I've seen kids cry over this game. I've seen parents rage over it.
Remember to hydrate. Water Bottles are free. Soda has a 10% discount for players.
Basic Hygiene Required.
Somebody built a stall deck specifically designed to make people rage-quit. Worked great, right up until the guy on the other end threw the table. We're getting a new table.
There's a fine line between 'clever stalling strategy' and 'actively trying to ruin someone's Tuesday.' I've had to explain that line to grown men.
Man hadn't showered since the regional qualifiers. I know because I could smell the regional qualifiers on him. Bathroom's right there. Please.
Had a guy build a deck with one purpose: waste everyone's time until they rage quit. Admire the commitment to villainy. Do not admire what came with it, smell-wise.
You can tell who's about to flip a table by how they start breathing through their nose. I keep a spare table now.
Somebody's stall strategy took forty-five minutes to lose one match on purpose. Guy left in tears. We have a turn timer now. You're welcome, everyone.
I don't ban people for playing to win. I ban people for playing to make someone else miserable. There's a real difference. Had to explain it with a whiteboard once.
Every shop's got a guy who smells like he sleeps in his car and plays like he's trying to get banned. Sometimes it's the same guy twice.
Had an actual physical fight over a stall deck once. Over a card game. Explained to the police this happens sometimes. They did not seem reassured.
Bring soap. Bring a deck that isn't designed to torture your opponent into quitting. That's really the whole membership policy.
Every collectible card game, every miniature line, every hobby that's ever had a competitive scene has had THIS guy. PixBots isn't special. We just get our own flavor of him.
Ran a different kind of card shop before this one. Different game, same guy. Same smell, even. It's honestly uncanny.
You'd think giant robot fights would draw a different crowd than trading cards. It does not. It is, somehow, the exact same five guys.

Talked to another shop owner at a convention once - different game entirely - and we realized we were describing the same customer. Word for word. There's a Platonic ideal of 'guy who ruins hobby shops' and he reincarnates into every genre.
There used to be a way to rig a Torso's whole weight into a drop-pod entrance. Players figured that out. Not the Corp. Guess what got patched first.
The community found a synergy loop the Corp never designed. It worked. It was beautiful. It lasted about two patches.

They banned a tile from Sanctioned play last patch. Doesn't matter it's the only mode it was ever legal in. Banned's banned. Somewhere there's a Legendary Splitter that just doesn't get to exist anymore.
Corp doesn't delete your parts. They just make every legal way to use them illegal. Same thing, more paperwork.
Corp did a full system rewrite two seasons back. Half the shop still plays the old ruleset on Sundays. I don't organize it. I definitely don't look the other way about it.
Official tournament rules say no unregistered part configs. I've never once checked anybody's grid that closely. Funny how that works.
If Corp asks, everyone here plays strictly by the book. If Corp doesn't ask, well, nobody's exactly checking hex grids at the door.
I don't work for the Corp. I sell their stuff and pay their licensing fee. That's the entire relationship. This shop is for you, not them.
Twenty years from now nobody remembers a quarterly balance patch. You'll remember who you played on a Tuesday. That's the whole point. The Corp will never get that. Good. Keep it that way.
The Corp thinks the game is the product. It's not. This room is the product. They just make the toys.
Corp sent another compliance memo. Filed it where I file all of them.
Your grid's a little too custom for a sanctioned bracket? I've got a drawer of boring, perfectly legal stock parts in back. Borrow what you need, give it back after.
Corp wants stock-only loadouts for the regional qualifier. Funny thing about my loaner bin - it's all stock. Every compliant piece. Doesn't mean I don't know whose real build is spicier.
I keep a full stock loadout in every slot, just for tournament day. Not because I care about the rule. Because I care about you actually getting to play.
You want to run your homebrew grid at home? Beautiful, keep doing that. Want to run it at Regionals and get DQ'd on a technicality? Come see me first.
Half my loaner bin exists so nobody gets locked out of a bracket over a part the Corp decided was 'non-standard' this month.
They keep asking for 'engagement telemetry.' I keep sending them attendance numbers and a shrug.
Every quarter the Corp finds a new way to make this hobby slightly more annoying to run. Every quarter, I find a new way to not let that reach you.
Corp's newsletter called last season's balance changes 'community-driven.' I was in the room. It was one guy in a meeting nobody attended.
I've got a filing cabinet just for Corp compliance paperwork. It's the heaviest thing in this building and it has never once helped a single kid win a match.
They rebranded the rulebook 'living document' this year. Every hobby shop owner I know translated that the same way: 'we'll change it whenever we feel like it.'
Corp's licensing terms say I have to display their logo 'prominently.' I hung it behind the mop bucket. Technically prominent.
You know what's never once come from the Corp? A good idea. Every good idea in this shop came from a kid with a weird build and too much free time.
I've watched three different 'official errata' walk back things players already fixed themselves, six months earlier, for free.
The rulebook update log this year is longer than the actual new content. Take from that what you will.
Corp keeps asking shop owners to 'self-report irregular play patterns.' I reported that my regulars have fun. Haven't heard back.
There's a version of the rules from three years ago I still trust more than the current one. I am not the only person who feels that way. I'm just the only one who admits it out loud.
A big part of running this place is translating Corp legalese into 'play however makes you happy, I won't tell.'
You'd think the people who made the game would trust the people who play it. You would, historically, be wrong about that.
The best builds in this shop's history never showed up in any Corp-sanctioned tier list. Make of that what you will.
Corp reissued the 'approved parts list' again. Third time this year. I've stopped printing it out. Waste of good paper.
I've got a drawer of 'discontinued' parts that work exactly the same as they always did. Discontinued means 'we stopped selling it,' not 'it stopped working.' I still let people use what they've got.
Some exec somewhere decided the shop-level tournament scene was getting 'too creative.' I decided that was the nicest thing anyone's said about you kids all year.
Corp's idea of listening to the community is a survey nobody asked for, about a change nobody wanted, that ships regardless of the answers.

The regional office called wanting to know why 'unsanctioned configurations' were still winning brackets at my shop. I told them I didn't know what they were talking about. I did know. I'm not a snitch.
You lose more hours to compliance paperwork running this place than to actual repairs. That should tell you everything about where the real problems in this hobby come from.
I've had the same argument with three different Corp reps over three different years about the same rule. I've won zero of those arguments and changed zero of my actual policies.
There's an official Corp position on homebrew parts. There's also what actually happens on my tables. I know which one the kids remember fondly.
Corp put out a statement calling last month's patch a 'quality of life pass.' Ask around. Nobody's life got any better.
I keep every old rulebook I've ever been issued. Not for nostalgia. For evidence, in case anyone ever asks me to explain myself.
Somebody complained the AI was 'too aggressive.' The AI is a training tool. It is supposed to be aggressive. That is the point of the tool.
Had a kid try to argue the rules with me for twenty minutes. I've run this shop for nine years. The rules have not changed in the last twenty minutes.
A parent asked if I could just 'let their kid win sometimes.' I told her the AI doesn't do favors and neither do the other regulars. Neither do I.
Somebody left a one-star review because their bot lost. The review was, and I quote, 'game bad, robot won.' I have it framed.
Had to institute a 'no throwing controllers' rule. I did not think that would need to be a rule. It needed to be a rule.
There's always one guy who thinks trash talk is a strategy. It is not a strategy. It is, however, a great way to get benched for a week.
Somebody tried to convince me their opponent 'cheated' by playing well. I explained the difference. He did not accept the explanation gracefully.
Had a kid cry because he lost. Had a grown man cry because he lost. Guess which one I was nicer to. It's not the one you think.
I don't mind sore losers. I mind LOUD sore losers. There is a very specific decibel line and several of you have found it.
Someone asked if we had a dress code. We don't. We should. I am considering it every single day.
A kid asked if he could bring his own 'lucky' controller. I said sure. It broke halfway through the match. It was not that lucky.
Had a customer demand a refund on a part because his bot still lost with it equipped. That is not how any of this works. I explained that. Slowly.
You'd be amazed how many arguments in this shop start with 'well ACTUALLY' and end with me explaining basic math.
Somebody accused a twelve-year-old of running a 'sweat build.' She's twelve. She's allowed to be good at the toy robot game. Let her cook.
Had a guy insist his loss was 'rigged.' The AI doesn't know your name. It has never once had an opinion about you personally. I checked.
There is a very fine gentleman's agreement in this shop that you don't gloat too hard. Most of you honor it. A few of you need reminders. Frequently.
Someone tried to bring their own snacks and I said fine, and then they left crumbs in the grid trays, and now nobody brings their own snacks.
Had a kid quit mid-match because he was 'obviously going to lose anyway.' You were not obviously going to lose. You were down by one life. Finish the game.
I've broken up more arguments over whose turn it was to use the demo table than over actual matches. People are strange about demo tables.
A regular asked me to ban his rival from the shop. His rival is eleven. I said no. They're friends again by the way. They're always friends again by Thursday.
Neighborhood Watch swept the block again last night. Nothing to report, allegedly. There's never anything to report. Funny how thorough 'nothing' requires being.
Had a knock on the back door at 2 AM. Corp logistics, unmarked van, wanted the thermal logs from the arena sensors. I gave them the logs. I always give them the logs.
Corp wants a 'field deployment readiness' report every quarter now. I write the same three sentences every time. They never ask me to elaborate.
There's a line-of-sight suppression clause buried in this year's licensing renewal. I read it twice. I still don't fully understand what it's for. I signed it anyway. You don't not-sign things.
Somebody official-looking asked about our 'unregistered building materials' inventory. I said it's a hobby shop, we have glue and cardboard. They wrote that down very seriously.
Power flickered twice last week during a match. Not a storm. No storm anywhere near here. I didn't ask. You learn not to ask.
Got an audit notice about 'non-standard thermal signatures' in the shop. I told them it's the microwave. It's mostly the microwave.
There's a new registration form for anyone bringing in outside hardware. I fill it out for you so you don't have to. Don't thank me. Just don't ask what happens to the copies.
A van sat outside for three hours yesterday. Didn't do anything. Just sat there. I brought them coffee around hour two. Seemed like the neighborly thing to do.
Corp's new terminology is 'field deployment readiness logs' instead of 'attendance sheet.' I don't love what that implies about what they think this is.
Somebody in a Corp jacket asked real specific questions about which of you win the most. I told him I don't keep those numbers. I keep those numbers. I did not give him those numbers.
The unmarked transport in the alley isn't new. I just never used to notice it. Funny what you start noticing after nine years of this.
Got asked to install a 'diagnostic sensor package' near the arena for 'quality assurance purposes.' It's in a box in my office. It stays in that box.
There's paperwork now for describing your bot's 'combat behavioral profile' in detail. I fill in the boring parts. I leave out the parts that make you special. Not their business.
Had someone from Corp ask, very casually, whether any of you show 'above-baseline tactical adaptation.' I said you're all just kids having fun. Which is also true.
I don't ask why the sensor sweep schedule changed. I don't ask why it changed again two weeks later. I just make sure none of you are here when it happens.

Somebody wanted copies of the AI's combat logs against our top players specifically. Not the bottom players. Not the average players. The top ones. I gave them nothing they couldn't already get from a leaderboard.
The shipment manifest this month has a line item I don't recognize and a delivery window I wasn't given. I signed for it anyway. Building's still standing.
Corp's asking shops to log 'novel tactical solutions' now. I told them innovation isn't really quantifiable. They disagreed. I filed it under things I'm ignoring.
There's a form for reporting 'unusual pilot aptitude.' I have never once filled it out completely. Some things are between me and the kid who earned it.
New shipment of paint came in. Half of it's already claimed. Speak now.
The vending machine's broken again. I've stopped fixing it. Consider it a permanent art installation.
Tuesday nights are quietest. Wednesday nights are FightShovel. Do the math on which one I prefer.
Somebody left a half-built bot on table six for THREE WEEKS. If that's you, come get it. I'm not running a storage unit.
We got a new poster for the wall. It's crooked. It's staying crooked. I like it crooked.
The coffee machine and I have an understanding. It makes bad coffee. I drink it anyway. That's a healthy relationship, I'm told.
Somebody asked if we sell replacement grid trays. We do. They're in the back. They're also overpriced, and I'm not sorry.
It's raining. The roof leaks over table three. I've known about this for six years. I have opinions about my own competence that I keep to myself.
New kid came in today, didn't say a word, built a genuinely solid starter loadout on the first try. Kept an eye on that one. You should too.
The shop cat has opinions about who's losing. She's usually right. I don't know how she does it.
Somebody asked why there's a 'no eating over the display case' sign. There's a story. The story is gross. Ask Silas.
Restocked the scrap bin this morning. It'll be picked clean by lunch. It's always picked clean by lunch.
The bell above the door's been broken for two weeks. I hear you come in anyway. Small shop. Good ears.
Somebody spilled soda in the demo unit. It still works. I don't recommend testing how long that'll stay true.
We're doing a scrap trade-in event this weekend. Bring your junk, leave with slightly less junk. Everybody wins, mostly me.
I've got a new shipment of chassis frames coming Thursday. Don't all show up at once. I know you will anyway.
The heater's fighting the AC again. Building's confused about the season. So am I, some days.
Somebody drew a pretty solid mural on the whiteboard instead of using it for match tracking. I left it up for a week out of respect.
Found a decade-old part in the back that shouldn't even still function. It still functions. Some things are just built right.
New rule: no more 'testing' the demo units at full volume during other people's matches. You know who you are.
The regulars have started a betting pool on match outcomes using scrap instead of money. I'm pretending not to notice. Mostly because I'm in it.
Somebody asked if the shop has a theme song. It does not. It should. I'm accepting submissions.
The FightShovel crowd and the PixBots crowd do not mix well on the same night. We learned that the hard way. We are not doing that again.
Got a new dartboard for the back room. It has never once been used for darts. I don't ask.
There's a very specific corner booth that's unofficially reserved for whoever just had the worst loss of the day. Everyone respects the corner booth.
The AC unit makes a noise like a dying robot. Given the context, nobody's ever once been alarmed by this.
Somebody left their jacket here three months ago. It's becoming part of the shop at this point. I've named it.
New batch of dice came in for the tabletop nights. Half of them are already suspiciously lucky. I don't ask questions about dice. Old shopkeeper rule.
Somebody asked to host a birthday party here. We did it. It went fine. We are doing it again, apparently, every year now.
The shop playlist is on shuffle. It has been on shuffle since we opened. I have never once skipped a song. Some traditions just happen.
Table four wobbles. Table four has always wobbled. Table four will always wobble. Put something under the leg or accept your fate.
Somebody's mom dropped off cookies for 'the whole gaming club.' There is no gaming club. There's just all of you. You ate the cookies anyway.
New display case arrived. It's for trophies. It is currently empty except for one very confident-looking rock someone put in there as a joke.
I keep meaning to repaint the sign out front. I keep not doing it. At this point it's basically vintage.
Had a slow Tuesday. Rearranged the shelves. You'll all complain that you can't find anything now. You'll get over it.
Somebody's little sibling wandered in and beat three regulars in a row on the demo unit. Nobody's talked about anything else all week.
The shop radio picked up static instead of music for an hour. Nobody noticed until I mentioned it. Make of that what you will about the ambiance.
New scented candle in the back office. It's called 'Garage.' It smells like ozone and regret. I love it.
Somebody brought their dad in to 'settle a rules dispute.' Dad had no idea what any of the rules were. Dad had opinions anyway. Dads are like that.
Got a delivery of replacement hex trays today. They're the good kind, not the cheap kind. Treat them better than you treat the cheap kind.
I keep the thermostat exactly one degree colder than comfortable. It's not an accident. It keeps matches moving.
Somebody proposed we do a 'no Mythic parts' casual night. We tried it. It lasted one night. Turns out you all really like your Mythic parts.
New arcade cabinet showed up in the corner. Don't ask where it came from. I didn't pay for it and I'm not giving it back.
Somebody asked if I ever get tired of this. Nine years in. Every single day's been different. No. Not yet. Ask me again in ten more.
The shop's had the same smell since the day I opened it. Ozone, solder, and old carpet. I wouldn't change a molecule of it.
Arthur showed up in a new jacket that costs more than my car again. Still can't out-tactic a decent flanking maneuver. Some things money just doesn't buy.
Beatrice left another notebook page on the counter. It's covered in equations I don't understand and one doodle of a very smug-looking bot.
Grog tried to fit through the front door sideways carrying his whole chassis. We're getting a bigger door. Eventually.
Leo and Luna showed up separately today, which never happens. Something's off. I'm choosing not to investigate.
Rudy asked me, very sincerely, if I've 'reconsidered my position on limiters.' I have not. I never will. He asks anyway. Every week.
Professor P. brought in a 'harmless' new compound for his bot's coating. The word 'harmless' has never once applied to anything Professor P. has brought in.
Zane blew through the shop so fast today I only know he was here because of the paperwork he left on the counter. Still don't know when he did that.
Chloe's swarm knocked over the scrap bin again. Again. I've started bolting things down specifically because of Chloe.
Vance sat in the corner reading for four hours without a single match. Said he was 'saving his shields for later.' Later never came. Vance is a mystery.
Maya showed up, set up in the exact corner she always sets up in, and didn't move for the entire session. I've started reserving that corner.
Declan rearranged half the demo tiles into some kind of trap formation 'just to see.' We're still finding pieces in weird spots.
Jin bet his own scrap against himself today. Lost both bets. Somehow still walked out ahead. I don't understand Jin's math and I've stopped trying.
Sammy brought in something he built out of what I'm fairly sure was a broken toaster. It won two matches. I have genuinely no explanation.
Rex spent twenty minutes today just watching someone else build before rebuilding his own bot to match. That kid has no shame and I respect it.
Hrothgar was explaining 'the old ways' of siege warfare to a very patient nine-year-old for forty-five minutes today. The nine-year-old won their match afterward. Make of that what you will.
Dan came in on his lunch break from the hardware store again, still in his work vest, still somehow undefeated. I don't get it either.
Evan showed up, said three words, and left. I don't know what those three words meant. I don't think I want to.
Arthur tried to buy his way to the front of the line for the demo table. I explained that's not how lines work. He was very confused by the concept.
Beatrice recalculated her whole build overnight after one loss. Came back with something scarier. I'm a little afraid of that notebook.
Grog and Dan had an arm-wrestling match that had nothing to do with the actual game. Grog won. Obviously.
The twins split up for once and both still won their matches independently. I don't know if that's more or less concerning.
Rudy's bot smoked so hard today the fire alarm almost went off. Almost. I've disabled the sensitivity on that thing specifically because of Rudy.
Professor P. asked to 'borrow' the mop bucket for 'research purposes.' I said no. He asked again. I said no again. This is an ongoing negotiation.
Zane tried to explain his build philosophy to a new kid. The explanation was faster than the build. Nobody understood a word.
Chloe's drone count keeps creeping up. I stopped asking where the extra ones come from around drone number fifteen.
Vance offered someone a free lesson in patience. The someone declined loudly and lost in four minutes. Vance didn't say 'I told you so.' I could tell he wanted to.
Maya hit three bots in a straight line today without moving an inch. The other regulars have started calling it 'the Maya special.' She seems fine with that.
Declan's magnet setup pulled someone's snack right off the table mid-match. He apologized. He did not stop doing it.
Jin flipped a coin before his match today 'for luck.' Lost the coin flip. Won the match anyway. Jin makes no sense and I've made peace with that.
Sammy's scrap-built bot finally fell apart mid-match. He rebuilt it in the parking lot with what I'm pretty sure was a bike chain. Different match, same day. Won that one too.
Shields regen faster if you stop taking hits for a second. Revolutionary concept, I know. Try it sometime.
Pierce ignores shields. Learn that the easy way or the hard way. I recommend the easy way.
Fire synergy burns over time. Patience is a valid damage strategy. Shocking, I know, for some of you.
Vortex pulls things toward the center. Stand near the center at your own risk.
A heavier bot turns slower. Physics doesn't care about your feelings. Neither do I, on this particular topic.
Overclocking your core is a real power boost and a real way to blow yourself up. Read the fine print. I mean it this time.
Splitters share energy across faces. Amplifiers make that energy hit harder. Combine them and stop asking me why your torso keeps melting.
The stealth bot doesn't actually vanish. It just gets quiet. Keep your ears open, not just your eyes.
Jammers mess with targeting, not movement. You can still walk out of a jammer field. Most people forget that mid-panic.
Cloak doesn't work if you're already shooting. Timing matters more than the tile itself.
A magnet build isn't just for loot. Ask Declan about repel mode sometime. Actually don't. He'll talk for an hour.
Poison stacks. Fire doesn't, as much. Mixing elements isn't just for flavor, it changes the math.
Kinetic tiles extend your range more than you'd think. Most people undervalue range until they don't have enough of it.
A drone bay is a second bot fighting for you. Treat it like one. Feed it a real loadout, not scraps.
Heal beacons work on you too, not just your team. Don't forget you're allowed to heal yourself.
The AI adapts to what beats it. Winning the same way twice in a row is asking for trouble.
Reflector tiles change direction, not power. Route smart, not just hard.
A torso needs room to fan power out. Don't cram your core into a corner and wonder why nothing reaches your arms.
Accumulators bank energy for a bigger hit later. Patience pays literal, mechanical dividends in this game.
Elemental resistance stacks per source. One strut won't save you. A few might.
Reactive plating only helps if something's close enough to hit back. It's a melee answer, not a ranged one.
Your build's mass affects your ramming damage. Heavier hits harder. Also turns slower. Pick your trade-off.
A Legendary part with a bad shape is still a bad shape. Rarity isn't everything. Geometry matters.
Watch your shield recharge delay before you go tanking hits on purpose. It's not free.
The meta shifts. What worked last week might not work this week. Adapt or lose gracefully. Preferably adapt.
You've come a long way since your first match. I still remember how bad that first bot was. I'm not going to describe it. Some things stay buried.
Every regular in this shop lost embarrassingly at some point. You included. It's not a scar. It's a rite of passage.
I don't say this to everybody, but you've got good instincts. Don't let it go to your head. I said 'good,' not 'perfect.'
You're starting to build like someone who's actually paying attention. That's rarer than you'd think.
I've watched a lot of pilots come through this shop. You're doing better than most at your stage. Keep that between us.
Somewhere along the way you stopped panicking mid-match. That's a bigger deal than winning. Losing calm is still progress.
You used to ask me for advice every match. Now you just nod and figure it out. That's the actual goal, kid.
I'm not handing out compliments for free today, but that was a genuinely smart play. There. Happy?
You've got a signature style now. I can tell your builds apart from everyone else's at a glance. That took work.
Every kid who's stuck with this hobby long enough eventually surprises me. You just did. Don't let it go to your head. Twice in one day is pushing it.
I've seen a hundred pilots quit after a bad week. You're still here. That matters more than any single match.
You handled that loss better than half the adults who come through here. I mean that as the compliment it is.
Watching you build has gotten genuinely fun to watch. That's not nothing, coming from someone who's watched this shop's worth of builds for nine years.
You ask better questions than you used to. That's the real tell that you're actually learning, not just winning.
I don't do participation trophies. I do genuine ones. That last run earned one.
You're going to look back at your early builds and cringe. Everyone does. Keep the cringe. It's proof of the distance traveled.
There's a version of you from a few months back that would not believe what you just pulled off. I believe it. Barely.
You stopped copying other people's builds a while back and started making your own mistakes. Better mistakes. Real progress looks like that.
I don't hand out 'I'm proud of you' lightly. Consider this one of the rare occasions.
Every pilot has a moment where the game clicks. I think I just watched yours happen in real time.
You've earned the right to ignore some of my advice now. Not all of it. Some.
The kid who walked in here your first day would not recognize the pilot standing in front of me now.
I keep a mental list of the regulars who actually improve instead of just grinding. You're on it. Don't tell the others.
That was the kind of comeback that gets talked about at the counter for a week. Enjoy it. You earned the gossip.
You've started teaching the newer kids without me asking. That's when I know someone's really part of this place.
I collect vintage repair manuals. Nobody asked. I'm telling you anyway.
My back hurts from bending over that workbench nine years running. Worth it. Mostly.
I used to pilot competitively myself, a long time ago. I'll tell that story when you've earned it. You haven't yet.
I have strong opinions about the correct way to store spare tiles. I will not be taking questions.
There's a specific mug behind the counter nobody's allowed to use. It's mine. It has always been mine. It will always be mine.
I don't believe in lucky numbers. I do believe in a lucky mug. See above.
Somebody asked what I do when the shop's closed. Mostly I fix things nobody asked me to fix. It's a compulsion at this point.
I've never once beaten Rudy in his prime. I'm not ashamed of that. Much.
I keep a spare of everything. Spare tiles, spare tables, spare patience. Especially the last one.
You'd think nine years of this would make me numb to a good comeback win. It has not. It never will.
I read the rulebook updates cover to cover every single time, out of spite mostly, at this point.
There's a photo behind the counter from the shop's first year. I will not be elaborating on the haircut.
I don't take days off during a big bracket week. My cat resents this. My cat resents most things.
Somebody asked if I ever get bored running this place. Nine years. Not once. Not even the slow Tuesdays.
I've got opinions about paint finishes that I will share whether you ask or not.
I keep the shop lights slightly dim on purpose. Makes the tile colors pop. Also saves on the electric bill. Both true.
There's a very specific way I like the scrap bin organized. Nobody follows it. I reorganize it every night anyway.
I've never missed an opening shift in nine years. I have missed several nights of sleep because of it. Trade-offs.
You'd be surprised how much of running a shop like this is just listening. I do more listening than talking, most days.
I keep every single 'thank you' note anyone's ever left at the counter. There's a whole shoebox. I'm not showing you the shoebox.
Somebody asked why I never expanded to a second location. One shop, done right, beats two done half right. That's the whole philosophy.
I've turned down offers to sell this place more than once. Never seriously considered any of them. Not once.
I don't do this job for the money. Correcting myself: I definitely don't do this job for the money.
There's a reason I never close early, even on slow nights. Somebody always shows up right at the wire needing a place to be.
I keep spare parts on hand for kids who can't afford a full kit yet. Don't make a thing of it. It's not a loan. Don't pay it back.
I've patched more scraped knees than actual bot parts around here, some weeks.
Every year I say I'll take a real vacation. Every year the bracket schedule says otherwise. I've made my peace with it.
This shop's outlived three other hobby stores on this block. I don't take that as luck. I take that as doing right by the people who walk in.
You ask me why I care so much about a toy robot fighting game. I'll tell you: it was never about the robots.
Nine years in, and the best part of this job is still watching a kid win their first real match. Every single time. No exceptions.
Somebody asked if the Corp ever visits in person. Once. Stayed twenty minutes. Left without buying anything. Never came back. I count that as a win.
New kid asked what happens if you lose too many matches in a row. I told her the truth: you build better and come back. That's the whole system.
A regular asked if there's a secret to beating the AI. There isn't. There's just paying attention and not panicking. That's the whole secret. Nobody believes me.
Somebody wanted to know my favorite build archetype. I don't have one. I have favorite PILOTS. The builds are just how they say hello.
Had someone ask if I ever get sick of watching the same matches over and over. No two matches are the same. Not once. Not in nine years.
You know it's a good week when the scrap bin's empty by Friday instead of Wednesday. This was a good week.
Somebody asked why the trophies aren't behind glass. Because you should be able to touch what you earned. That's not up for debate.
New synergy interaction dropped this patch. Half the shop's already theorycrafting. I love this part of the job.
A kid asked if I ever get tired of explaining the same rule for the hundredth time. Every rule explained is one more person who gets to actually play. Worth it every time.
Somebody left a thank-you drawing taped to the register. It's staying there. Forever. Deal with it.
I've got a running tally of how many times someone's said 'just one more match' and meant it. The number is a lie every single time. Including yours. Especially yours.
You know your shop's doing something right when the regulars start bringing their siblings. Half my new pilots this year came in that way.
Somebody asked if there's a max skill level. There isn't. There's just how much further you're willing to push. I've seen it go pretty far.
A parent thanked me for 'keeping their kid off the streets.' I didn't have the heart to explain what's actually happening outside those streets these days. Some things stay unsaid.
I keep this place brighter than it needs to be and warmer than it needs to be. On purpose. You'll understand why eventually. Maybe you already do.
Somebody asked why I never franchise. This shop only works because I know every single one of your names. That doesn't scale. I like that it doesn't scale.
New kid's first build was rough. Everybody's first build is rough. That's not a criticism. That's just Tuesday.
I keep a chalkboard just for kill counts and personal records. It's getting full. I need a bigger chalkboard. I'm not buying a bigger chalkboard. Some things stay the way they started.
Had a slow morning, reorganized the tile bins by color instead of type. You'll all hate it. I'll switch it back by Friday. I do this sometimes.
You know a build's good when even Beatrice stops to watch it work. That happened today. Write it down somewhere.
Somebody asked if the shop's ever been robbed. Once. They took the register and left every single bot part untouched. Say what you want about criminals, apparently some of them have standards.
New batch of paint dried weird. Half-batch of very good-looking mistakes. I'm selling them as 'limited edition.' Marketing is mostly just confidence.
A kid asked if losing gets easier. No. It gets more useful. That's different from easier and it's the only honest answer I've got.
Somebody wanted to know the fastest anyone's ever won a match here. I'm not telling you. It'll just make you try something stupid.
I've started keeping earplugs behind the counter. Not for the noise. For Grog's victory shouting. Mostly for that.
Every shop's got a wall of shame and a wall of fame. Mine's the same wall. Depends which day you ask me which is which.
You ever notice the shop's never actually empty, even on the slowest nights? Someone's always here. That's not an accident either.
Somebody asked if I miss piloting myself. Some days. Mostly I like this better. Watching you all get good at it scratches the same itch.
New kid nearly cried asking if they were 'bad at this.' They are not bad at this. They are new at this. Those are different words for a reason.
I've never once regretted opening this place. Bad days, sure. Regret, never.
first_boss_intro: Heads up — that's a Corp centerpiece model. They ship one big chassis per trainer kit so new pilots learn to fight something SCARY. Kill the legs out from under the drama.
first_boss_defeat: And THAT is why we keep the good salvage behind the counter. Take your pick, champ.
boss_defeats: Down goes the big one! Somebody get the broom.
Corp's gonna want that chassis back. Corp can have it in pieces.
You know some regulars practice a month before their first centerpiece kill? Don't tell them how fast you got yours.
That was a lot of expensive hardware you just turned into scrap. Good job.
I'd ask if you're proud of yourself, but I can see the smirk from here.
Another centerpiece goes to the junkyard. I hope the Corp has good insurance.
You took that thing apart like it was made of cheap plastic. Which it might be.
Nice maneuvering. I thought you were toast when it charged.
You're making the AI look bad. It's going to hold a grudge.
I'm going to need a bigger scrap bin.
That boss had a family. Mostly smaller, equally angry bots, but still.
I almost felt bad for it. Almost.
Textbook takedown. You've been doing your homework.
I think I saw a spark of genuine fear in its optical sensors.
Keep playing like that and I'll have to start charging you for the electricity.
You just voided its warranty in record time.
If anyone asks, that crater was already there.
That's one way to disassemble a multi-million dollar prototype.
You're going to need a bigger trophy shelf.
I'm not saying I'm impressed, but my eyebrow is slightly raised.
That boss thought it was the apex predator. You proved it wrong.
Clean kill. The AI is frantically rewriting its combat algorithms right now.
I guess the Corp needs to go back to the drawing board on that model.
You dismantled that thing with the cold efficiency of a tax auditor.
I've seen worse pilots survive longer, but not many.
That was a solid hit. You actually made me look up from my magazine.
The bigger they are, the more salvage they drop.
I hope you got a good picture of that explosion. It was cinematic.
You're starting to look like a real pilot out there.
That boss was a menace. Now it's a paperweight.
I'll add that kill to the chalkboard. It's getting full.
You just gave that AI a complex. It's going to need therapy.
Not bad. Not bad at all. Now do it again.

Arthur.intro: Arthur just walked in. His parents bought him the entire new set before it officially released. His bot is basically a walking vault of Mythic parts. Try to scratch the paint.
Arthur.win: Money can't buy tactical awareness! Arthur's having his chauffeur carry out the pieces.
Arthur.loss: Yeah, there's a reason those parts cost more than my car. Better luck next time.
Arthur.gimmick: Only uses the most expensive, rarest Mythic parts. Raw stats over synergy.

monologues.round_1: Don't touch the paint, peasant. Do you know how much a single Mythic actuator costs? More than your whole garage.
monologues.round_2: You got lucky last time. My chassis wasn't polished. Let's see you handle the real power of money.
monologues.round_3: I don't care how many matches you've won, you're still using scraps. I'm going to put you in your place.
monologues.mythic: Okay... I admit it. You've got skills. Even my dad's corporate engineers couldn't build a loadout like yours. Show me how you do it.

Beatrice.intro: Beatrice wants a match. She's been doing calculations in a notebook for an hour. Her bot isn't just built, it's engineered. Watch out for chain reactions.
Beatrice.win: You just broke her algorithm! She's furiously erasing equations right now.
Beatrice.loss: Mathematically eliminated. She predicted your every move on page four.
Beatrice.gimmick: Perfect mathematical synergy. Every part triggers a reaction in another part.

monologues.round_1: Your build is highly inefficient. I've calculated fourteen distinct structural flaws. Prepare to be optimized out of the bracket.
monologues.round_2: I had to carry a remainder in my last equation to account for your... erratic playstyle. I won't make that mistake twice.
monologues.round_3: Your loadout defies traditional mathematical models. It's fascinating. I'd like to test a new theorem against it.

Grog.intro: Here comes Grog. He calls his bot 'The Blender.' He doesn't believe in ranged weapons or dodging. Keep your distance, or you'll get pureed.
Grog.win: The bigger they are, the harder they crash! Good job kiting the big guy.
Grog.loss: Well... your bot is flat now. We'll need a spatula.
Grog.gimmick: Pure, unadulterated melee aggression. Heavy armor, massive physical damage.

monologues.round_1: Me smash your little toy into tiny pieces! Grog strongest!
monologues.round_2: You run fast. But Grog smash faster this time!
monologues.round_3: You tough. You take big hit and not break. Grog respect that. Let us have good smash!

Leo & Luna.intro: Oh boy. The twins are challenging you. It's a 2v1. One of them is going to stab you in the back while the other shoots you from across the room. I'm legally obligated to say: Good luck.
Leo & Luna.win: You beat the twins?! And you watched your own back! That's... genuinely impressive.
Leo & Luna.loss: You didn't see that coming, did you? Neither did I, and I have the security cameras.
Leo & Luna.gimmick: A 2v1 match. Luna uses a cloaked melee assassin; Leo uses a cloaked long-range sniper.

monologues.round_1: (Leo) "They won't even see us coming." (Luna) "They never do, brother. It's almost too easy."
monologues.round_2: (Leo) "You survived the crossfire last time." (Luna) "An anomaly. We've adjusted our firing arcs."
monologues.round_3: (Leo) "You have eyes in the back of your head." (Luna) "A worthy prey. Let us dance in the shadows once more."

Rudy.intro: It's Rudy. He was the best pilot in this shop three years ago. Then he started... experimenting. Bypassing safety limiters. Overclocking. His bot is a ticking bomb. Don't let it take you with it.
Rudy.win: Rudy's bot finally melted down. A tragedy, really, but a win's a win.
Rudy.loss: He might be crazy, but the power output on that thing is undeniable. Get the fire extinguisher.
Rudy.gimmick: The Overclocker. Used to be the shop champion until he started tampering with his core. His bot deals massive, erratic damage but damages itself over time. Unstable.

monologues.round_1: Limiters are for cowards! You're gonna see true power! Assuming my core doesn't melt first!
monologues.round_2: I tweaked the plasma regulator! It's running at 400% capacity! It burns! It burns so good!
monologues.round_3: You're crazy. You're crazier than me. You stare down the meltdown and you don't even blink. Let's see who burns out first!

Professor P..intro: Professor P. is up. He doesn't do direct damage. He just applies layers of acid and fire until there's nothing left. Try not to inhale the fumes.
Professor P..win: You extinguished his thesis! Excellent counter-play.
Professor P..loss: You've been successfully dissolved. Let me get the mop.
Professor P..gimmick: Status effects. Acid, Fire, Shock. Wants to watch you slowly melt.

monologues.round_1: Ah, a new specimen. Let's observe how your armor plating reacts to a concentrated sulfuric compound.
monologues.round_2: Your resistance to corrosive agents was statistically anomalous. I've prepared a more volatile mixture for this experiment.
monologues.round_3: Your adaptations are nothing short of brilliant. This next match will be published in my most prestigious journal!

Zane.intro: Zane's up. If you blink, his bot has already crossed the board twice. Don't try to track him, anticipate where he's going.
Zane.win: You caught the fly! Precision beats speed when it matters.
Zane.loss: Death by a thousand very, very fast papercuts.
Zane.gimmick: All jump-jets and haste engines. Fragile but almost impossible to hit.

monologues.round_1: Try to keep up! Actually, don't. It's embarrassing to watch you try.
monologues.round_2: You managed to clip my wing last time. I've upgraded my thrusters. You won't even see the blur.
monologues.round_3: You've got fast reflexes. Real fast. Most people give up. Let's push the redline and see who breaks.

Chloe.intro: Chloe's challenging you. She never fights alone. Expect about twenty micro-bots to swarm the field before you can say 'pest control.'
Chloe.win: Swarm defeated! It's like stepping on a nest of angry, robotic hornets.
Chloe.loss: You got overrun. There's just too many of them.
Chloe.gimmick: Minion spam. Summons turrets, tiny drones, and decoys.

monologues.round_1: Why fight alone when you can bring friends? And by friends, I mean thirty autonomous kill-drones.
monologues.round_2: You squashed my little ones. They didn't like that. And neither did I.
monologues.round_3: You handle the swarm better than anyone. My drones actually consider you an apex threat now. I'm honored.

Vance.intro: Vance is here. He built a fortress, not a fighter. It's going to be a long, slow grind. Bring a book.
Vance.win: The walls came tumbling down! Nice siege tactics.
Vance.loss: You ran out of ammo and he's still at full shields. Classic Vance.
Vance.gimmick: Ultimate defense. Shields, barricades, repair drones. Wins by outlasting you.

monologues.round_1: Go ahead. Shoot me. I've got all day. My shields recharge faster than you can pull the trigger.
monologues.round_2: You found a crack in the armor. Impressive. But I brought the heavy barricades this time.
monologues.round_3: You're the unstoppable force, and I'm the immovable object. This is what we play the game for.

Maya.intro: Maya's set up in the corner. If you walk into a straight line, she'll put a hole through three of your bots at once. Stay in cover.
Maya.win: You closed the gap! A sniper's worst nightmare is a melee weapon.
Maya.loss: You caught a railgun round to the core. Next time, zig-zag.
Maya.gimmick: Plays from the absolute furthest edge of the board. Piercing railguns.

monologues.round_1: Distance is safety. By the time you figure out where I am, there'll be a hole through your chassis.
monologues.round_2: You're good at closing the gap. I respect that. But I've recalibrated my optics.
monologues.round_3: I don't usually let anyone get this close. You've earned the right to see the whites of my eyes.

Declan.intro: Watch your step. Declan uses the board itself as a weapon. If you get pulled into a corner, you aren't coming out.
Declan.win: You avoided the traps and took him out! Great spatial awareness.
Declan.loss: You walked right into that one. Literally.
Declan.gimmick: Magnet tiles, push/pull mechanics, hazards. Uses the arena against you.

monologues.round_1: Watch your step. The board is mine. Every tile is a trap waiting to snap.
monologues.round_2: You sidestepped the magnets. Clever. But I've rigged the entire quadrant this time.
monologues.round_3: You read the board like a grandmaster. It's a genuine pleasure trying to outsmart you.

Jin.intro: Jin plays the odds. His bot is chaotic and unpredictable. Even he doesn't know what it's going to do. Roll the dice.
Jin.win: The house always wins, and today, you're the house.
Jin.loss: He rolled a natural twenty on that plasma blast. Pure luck. Probably.
Jin.gimmick: RNG parts. Attacks might do 1 damage or 100 damage. Teleports randomly.

monologues.round_1: Snake eyes or jackpot, let's let the dice decide! I love the thrill of the unknown!
monologues.round_2: My luck ran dry last hand. But the house always takes another bet. Double or nothing!
monologues.round_3: You don't play the odds, you make your own luck. That's the mark of a true high roller. Deal me in!

Sammy.intro: Sammy built his bot out of the scrap bin I keep out back. It shouldn't function, but it does. Don't underestimate the junk.
Sammy.win: You sent him back to the scrapyard. Good.
Sammy.loss: Defeated by literal trash. I won't tell anyone if you won't.
Sammy.gimmick: Built entirely from rusted, junkyard parts that have bizarre, unintended interactions.

monologues.round_1: One man's trash is my treasure! Don't laugh at the rust, it adds character!
monologues.round_2: I found a shiny new exhaust pipe in the dumpster. It makes my bot 12% more unpredictable!
monologues.round_3: You don't care that my bot is made of cans and duct tape. You fight me like a pro. Thanks for not going easy on me.

Rex.intro: Hold up. Rex wants a match. He's been staring at your bot for twenty minutes. He just rebuilt his to match yours, piece for piece. Let's see who pilots it better.
Rex.win: You proved you're the original! Nobody flies your rig like you do.
Rex.loss: Losing to your own build hurts. He's going to be so smug about this.
Rex.gimmick: He analyzes your exact build and copies it, but he's practiced with it against the AI.

monologues.round_1: Anything you can do, I can do better. Let's see how you handle your own medicine.
monologues.round_2: So you tweaked your build. Cute. I downloaded your new schematic ten minutes ago.
monologues.round_3: You've mastered this loadout. I can copy the parts, but I can't copy your instincts. Show me the masterclass.

Hrothgar.intro: Hrothgar runs the historical wargaming nights - Thursdays, if you're ever free. Doesn't talk much until the bot's actually dented. Then he won't shut up. Something about 'the old ways.' Keep moving. I mean that literally - keep MOVING.
Hrothgar.win: You never let him get a mortar to land clean. Smart. Ask him about it after - he loves explaining exactly how you won.
Hrothgar.loss: There it is. The big one. I've seen it land a hundred times and it still gets me.
Hrothgar.gimmick: Huge AoE mortars - fireball energy, not melee. Lobs slow, telegraphed, devastating area blasts rather than chasing you down; the threat is standing in the wrong place, not getting caught by him directly. Keeps a thread of the "ancient warfare" framing (a wizard who studies siege history, not just spellbooks) and the escalation idea from the original draft - his mortars get bigger/more frequent the longer the fight runs, like he's building toward something.

monologues.round_1: You fight like the moderns do. All caution, no conviction. Artillery doesn't care about conviction.
monologues.round_2: You're learning the blast radius. Good. I've adjusted it.

Dan.intro: This is Dan. He works at the hardware store two doors down. Never bought a Mythic part in his life. Hits like he's still mad about something from 2019. Nobody can explain how he's undefeated in this bracket. I've stopped trying.
Dan.win: You beat Dan. I don't - I genuinely don't know what to tell you. Nobody's done that.
Dan.loss: Common parts. Uncommon pilot. That's the whole secret and it's still not enough for most people.
Dan.gimmick: Starter-tier gear, zero customization, zero Mythic parts, full aggression - wins purely on positioning and timing, not power. Reads as pure unga-bunga simplicity on paper and is a real problem in practice.

monologues.round_1: Nice bot. Real nice. Mine's the starter frame. Let's see which one of us actually knows how to use theirs.
monologues.round_2: You're better than last time. I'm exactly the same. That's kind of the point.
monologues.round_3: Honestly? This is the most fun I've had all week. Don't tell my wife I said that about a hobby.

Evan.intro: ...I don't actually know Evan. He just started showing up. Says he's 'evaluating the venue.' Nobody invited him. He knows an unusual amount about your last three builds. I'd ask him about it, but something about how he says 'that's not important right now' keeps me from following up.
Evan.win: Evan packs up without a word. Doesn't seem upset. Writes something down. I really don't like that guy.
Evan.loss: Well. He knew exactly how to beat you before you even queued up. Make of that what you will.
Evan.gimmick: Deliberately UNDER-powers every shot instead of racing for bigger ones - low individual damage, constant chip-fire, evasive, hard to pin down. First concrete face on the dystopian-hints thread (see the Worldbuilding section below) - his whole kit is built around staying under whatever threshold keeps a sensor sweep from flagging him.

monologues.round_1: Interesting build. Interesting history, too. I've read the whole file.
monologues.round_2: You adapted. Noted. I'll adjust the file.
monologues.round_3: You're better than the file suggested. That's... actually a problem for someone. Not for me.

Joe.gimmick: Not fully worked out yet - the seed idea is a build that routes/uses hex tiles in configurations nobody else would, getting value out of "wrong" placements the solver/meta would never suggest. May get bespoke part geometry (a shape or footprint no other loadout has access to) as his signature edge, on top of the unconventional-usage angle. Needs a real design pass before this is playable - captured here as direction, not a finished kit.

Frank.intro: Look. I wasn't going to do this. But you cleared the others, and there's a rule - shop owner's gotta close out the bracket personally, or the trophy doesn't count. Full disclosure: I've been taking notes since your first wave. Might've built something that knows your bot a little too well.
Frank.win: ...Yeah. Okay. That's - that's fair. That's a fair win. Go put it on the chalkboard yourself, I need a minute.
Frank.loss: Come on now. I run this place. Did you think I just watch you all day for fun? ...Okay, partially for fun.
Frank.gimmick: Adaptive/mirror build with a support-caster's ear for a room - he's been quietly taking notes on the player's own dominant synergy/element all game (and, bard-style, seems to know a little about everyone else's builds too) and built something that specifically counters it. The Director's own evolution trick, but personal.

monologues.round_1: Nine years of watching people build. I've picked up a thing or two. Let's see if I remember how to actually pilot one of these.
monologues.round_2: You've got a tell. Everyone does. I've just had more time to notice yours than most.

travelling_champion.intro: Now THIS is an occasion. A travelling champion's AI, fresh off someone else's table, somewhere out there in the world. Different shop, different habits, different homework. Beat the ghost, take the glory.
travelling_champion.win: I'm putting this on the board out front. 'LOCAL PILOT DEFEATS [CHAMPION_NAME].' You want that in marker or the good vinyl letters?
travelling_champion.loss: Their table taught them different tricks, that's all. Study the War Room tape and issue a rematch. Champions love rematches. It's why they travel.

generic_rival_wins: Clean match! Shake the hand, take the win.
You out-piloted them. Plain and simple.
They had a good build, but your strategy was better.
That's another notch on your belt. Don't let it go to your head.
You read them like an open book. Good tactical awareness.
They thought they had the counter, but you adapted perfectly.
A solid victory. They're going to be analyzing that replay for hours.
You dismantled their game plan. Excellent work.
You proved your loadout is superior. At least for today.
A well-earned win. Now go claim your salvage.
They put up a fight, but you had the edge.
You stayed cool under pressure. That's what wins matches.
They're walking away with a bruised ego and a broken bot.
You just sent them back to the drawing board.
generic_rival_losses: Losing is just a lesson with a higher repair bill.
They outplayed you this time. Figure out why, and don't let it happen again.
You got outmaneuvered. It happens to the best of us.
Their build was a hard counter. Time to tweak your loadout.
You missed a crucial opening. Pay closer attention next time.
They saw right through your strategy. You need to be more unpredictable.
A tough loss, but a valuable one. Review the tape.
They had the better tactics today. Tomorrow is a new day.
You got caught off guard. Stay frosty.
Your bot wasn't ready for that kind of punishment. Upgrade your armor.
They exploited a weakness you didn't even know you had.
You hesitated. In this game, hesitation is scrap.
They brought a better tool for the job. Adapt and overcome.
You got steamrolled. Dust yourself off and get back to the garage.
Losing stings, but it's the only way to get better. Go fix your bot.

milestones.10_bosses: Ten centerpiece kills. That's Sponsored Pilot tier — Corp merch box, don't ask me what shipping cost. One Legendary chassis piece, two Legendary tiles. Spend them loud.
milestones.level_100: Kid. Level one hundred. I've had the shop nine years and I've rarely seen a pilot reach this point. Based on your record and how much you've forced the AI to evolve, the system's authorizing a payout. I'm looking at up to fifteen Mythic tiles for you. Fifteen. Corp says 'tournament-grade.' I say try not to vaporize my east wall.

black_market: Officially, that case is 'returns pending inspection.' Unofficially — players sell to each other. That kid, Silas? He always has the strangest, glitchiest, non-regulation components. I don't know where he gets them, and the rotation changes every ten minutes. Nothing has a warranty. You didn't hear it from me.
death_footers: Bots break. Pilots learn. Bench is that way, I'll put the kettle on.
The trainer got you. The trainer gets everyone. It's the learning part of the learning tool.
That arm's fixable. Your pride, also fixable. Scrap's in the bin.
Don't let it get to your head. I lost my first twenty matches in a row.
Go tweak your loadout. A minor adjustment is the difference between scrap and glory.
You're getting predictable. The AI learns. You have to learn faster.
game_over_3_loss: Three straight losses in the brackets. Look, kid, I'm sorry... but Corp rules are Corp rules. I have to pull your tournament registration for this circuit. Take some time, build a new rig, and we'll try again next season.
tournament_teaser: You've seen the bracket out front, right? Regional qualifiers run through sponsored shops like mine. Keep this up and I'm signing you up — and I do NOT put my shop's name on just anybody. Ask Rudy... Actually, don't ask Rudy. Just keep winning.

boss_rush.intro: So, you want to run the gauntlet. No breaks, no easy waves, just the heavy hitters back to back. If you survive, you keep what you salvage. If you don't... well, let's hope you survive.
boss_rush.completion: You actually cleared the board. I don't think I've seen anyone do that since Rudy before... well, never mind. Take your loot, you earned every piece.
